message.content:
I don’t have real‑time data, but you can quickly check the current air quality in Los Angeles on a few reliable sites:

| Source | How to use |
|--------|------------|
| **AirNow** (U.S. EPA) | Go to [airnow.gov](https://www.airnow.gov/), enter “Los Angeles” or your ZIP code, and view the AQI (Air Quality Index) and pollutant breakdown. |
| **AQICN** (World Air Quality Index) | Visit [aqicn.org](https://aqicn.org/city/los-angeles/). It shows the AQI, main pollutants, and a forecast. |
| **Local news apps** | Many local news outlets (e.g., LA Times, KABC) have live air‑quality widgets. |
| **Weather apps** | Apps like Weather.com, AccuWeather, or the built‑in weather app on iOS/Android often display AQI for major cities. |

**What to look for:**

- **AQI value**: 0–50 (Good), 51–100 (Moderate), 101–150 (Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups), 151–200 (Unhealthy), 201–300 (Very Unhealthy), 301+ (Hazardous).
- **Primary pollutant**: PM₂.₅, PM₁₀, O₃, NO₂, SO₂, CO.
- **Health advice**: If the AQI is above 100, sensitive groups (children, elderly, people with respiratory conditions) should limit outdoor activity.

If you need a quick snapshot right now, you can also ask a smart assistant (Google Assistant, Siri, Alexa) or check the “Air Quality” widget on your phone’s home screen.
